d: CARMA is a globally-trusted media intelligence leader with decades of experience helping PR and communications professionals monitor what matters, measure what’s meaningful, and demonstrate the value of their work. We combine cutting-edge technology, including AI-enabled media monitoring across print, online, broadcast, and social channels in 100+ languages - with deep human expertise to deliver actionable insights that inform strategy and drive business-critical decisions. With a diverse global team supporting thousands of organizations worldwide, CARMA empowers partners to turn complex media data into clarity and context, elevate the impact of earned media, and deepen understanding of stakeholder influence across markets.
We are looking for a Chief Accountant to take ownership of the day-to-day accounting, monthly management accounts, statutory compliance, and balance sheet integrity of our UAE entity.

Based in Dubai, the role reports to the Head of Finance and will act as the primary finance owner on the ground, responsible for delivering a clean and timely month-end close in line with the Group timetable, maintaining strong financial controls, and ensuring all UAE tax and statutory obligations are met.

You will work within an international, multi-currency environment, primarily across AED, USD, GBP and EUR, reporting under IFRS and collaborating closely with the wider Group Finance, FP&A, payroll, tax, and operational teams.
q: Strong practical knowledge of UAE accounting, VAT, Corporate Tax, and statutory compliance requirements.
Good understanding of IFRS, particularly IFRS 15 Revenue Recognition and IFRS 16 Leases.
Qualified or finalist accountant such as ACCA, ACA, CIMA, CPA, CMA, CA, or equivalent professional qualification.
Approximately 5+ years of accounting experience, including strong exposure to management accounting, month-end close, and financial reporting.
Previous experience working in a Chief Accountant, Senior Accountant, Management Accountant, or similar role.
Experience preparing complete monthly management accounts, balance sheet reconciliations, and financial analysis.
Experience with intercompany accounting, related-party transactions, and multi-currency environments.
Experience supporting or managing external audits.
Strong understanding of accounts receivable, accounts payable, cash flow, and working-capital management.
Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or a comparable ERP system is preferred.
Fluent English is required, as this is the working language of the Group.
Strong attention to detail with a high level of accuracy and financial discipline.
Self-sufficient, organised, and deadline-driven, with the ability to manage the UAE finance function
Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both finance and non-finance stakeholders across different locations.
r: Prepare monthly management accounts, including P&L, balance sheet and cash flow , for the UAE entity in line with the Group close timetable.

Deliver accurate month-end submissions to the London-based Finance Business Partner in the required Group reporting format, including variance analysis and commentary against budget, forecast, and prior year.
Prepare and post month-end journals, including accruals, prepayments, deferred revenue, payroll, depreciation, provisions, and IFRS 16 lease accounting entries .
Maintain complete monthly balance sheet reconciliations , including ageing and timely clearance of reconciling items.
Review the general ledger and ensure all transactions are correctly classified, supported, and recorded.
Support the annual budgeting and periodic forecasting processes in collaboration with the Finance Business Partner and FP&A team.
Ensure month-end and year-end close activities are completed accurately and within agreed deadlines.
Maintain deferred and accrued revenue schedules for annual, subscription-based, monitoring, and project-based contracts in accordance with IFRS 15 .
Ensure customer billing is complete, accurate, and recorded in the correct accounting period.
Review revenue recognition across different service arrangements, including subscriptions, reporting services, and ad-hoc projects.
Track and accrue third-party content, supplier, technology, and data-platform costs, ensuring costs are recognised in the appropriate period.
Monitor gross margin by client and service line , investigating significant movements and highlighting potential margin erosion to the Finance Business Partner.
Review supplier invoices and expenses to ensure correct coding, supporting documentation, and appropriate approvals.
Own the UAE finance compliance calendar and ensure all required filings and payments are completed accurately and on time.
Prepare and coordinate UAE VAT returns , ensuring accurate treatment of output VAT, input VAT, reverse-charge transactions, and supporting documentation.
Maintain appropriate VAT records and reconciliations and coordinate with external tax advisors where required.
Support the preparation of the Company's UAE Corporate Tax calculations, returns, supporting schedules, and tax reconciliations.
Maintain appropriate accounting records and documentation to support Corporate Tax positions and potential Federal Tax Authority reviews.
Monitor related-party and intercompany transactions from a UAE transfer-pricing perspective and maintain appropriate supporting documentation in coordination with Group Finance and external advisors.
Support compliance with applicable UAE accounting, tax, company, and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate regulatory or corporate filings with the Company's local corporate services provider or relevant authority, as applicable.
Keep up to date with changes in UAE accounting and tax regulations and highlight relevant changes to Group Finance.
Coordinate monthly payroll accounting with HR and the payroll provider.
Review payroll journals, employee benefits, leave provisions, bonuses, end-of-service benefit provisions, and other employee-related liabilities.
Reconcile payroll records to the general ledger each month.
Support payroll payment processes and Wages Protection System (WPS) requirements where applicable.
Ensure employee-related accruals and provisions are appropriately recorded in accordance with UAE requirements and Group accounting policies.
Reconcile all intercompany balances with Group entities each month and resolve differences before month-end close.
Process Group cost allocations, management charges, and recharge entries in accordance with Group policies and transfer-pricing arrangements.
Maintain appropriate supporting documentation for intercompany transactions.
Manage foreign exchange revaluation of monetary balances across AED, USD, GBP, EUR, and other relevant currencies.
Review foreign exchange gains and losses and ensure appropriate accounting treatment.
Work closely with Group Finance to ensure UAE reporting is aligned with Group accounting policies and IFRS requirements.
Prepare statutory financial statements and supporting schedules in accordance with IFRS and applicable UAE requirements .
Coordinate the annual external audit and act as the main finance contact for local auditors.
Own and coordinate audit PBC (Prepared by Client) requests , ensuring documentation is provided accurately and on time.
Support Group auditors during interim and year-end audit processes.
Maintain effective internal financial controls and ensure compliance with Group finance policies and the Delegation of Authority.
Identify control gaps or accounting risks and recommend appropriate improvements.
Monitor accounts receivable and support the collection of outstanding customer balances.
Prepare monthly reporting on DSO, overdue balances, and collection status .
Prepare short-term cash-flow forecasts and flag potential funding requirements to the Finance Business Partner in advance.
Monitor bank balances and complete monthly bank reconciliations.
Manage supplier payment runs, ensuring payments have appropriate supporting documentation and approvals.
Liaise with banks and internal stakeholders regarding routine banking and payment matters when required.
Maintain accurate accounting records within the Company's ERP system.
Support improvements to month-end reporting, reconciliations, financial controls, and accounting processes.
Identify opportunities to automate manual finance processes and improve reporting efficiency.
Work closely with Finance colleagues across different countries to standardise processes and support Group-wide finance initiatives.

d: Goodman Masson is partnering with a new financial markets venture under formation in Oman. Backed by prominent institutional investors, the business is building its operations from the ground up and is now hiring during the build phase.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced financial services lawyer to establish and lead the legal function of a new, licensed multi-asset market infrastructure. Operating within a financial centre founded on a common law framework, the business is developing its legal, regulatory and operational foundations ahead of its planned launch.

The successful candidate will play a central role in establishing the legal basis on which the infrastructure operates, ensuring the enforceability of book-entry title, settlement finality and participant obligations. This is a senior position requiring specialist knowledge of financial market infrastructure, securities settlement and regulatory frameworks, alongside the ability to build a legal function from a blank page.

Reporting to the Programme Director, you will establish and lead the company's legal function, taking ownership of its legal framework, regulatory engagement, participant documentation and material commercial contracts.

You will act as the company's principal legal interface with regulators, market participants, external counsel and infrastructure providers. Working closely with the wider programme team, you will ensure that the legal foundations are robust, enforceable and appropriate for a licensed market infrastructure operating across multiple asset classes and jurisdictions.
This is an opportunity to shape the legal framework of a new institution rather than inherit an established function.
q: Qualified lawyer in a common-law jurisdiction, such as England and Wales or an equivalent jurisdiction, holding a current practising certificate.
At least 10 years' post-qualification experience, including a minimum of 5 years specialising in financial market infrastructure or post-trade.
Direct experience of securities settlement, custody or registry infrastructure, gained within an infrastructure operator, regulatory authority or through advising such organisations.

Strong working knowledge of the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI), particularly the legal basis, settlement finality, money settlements, central securities depositories and operational risk.
Experience drafting, negotiating or providing legal opinions on settlement finality and book-entry title regimes, ideally across multiple jurisdictions.
Experience leading or co-leading a regulatory authorisation or recognition application and managing an ongoing supervisory relationship.
Proven experience drafting rulebooks and participation agreements and negotiating these with banks, custodians and their legal advisers.
Experience negotiating material outsourcing and technology contracts for regulated financial services businesses.
Exceptional legal drafting skills, with the ability to produce clear, robust documentation to an English common-law standard.
The professional judgement and integrity to challenge proposed approaches where they are not supported by the law, including at senior level.
Experience working within a GCC financial free zone or comparable common-law financial centre, such as DIFC, ADGM or AIFC.
Exposure to Islamic finance structures, sukuk documentation and Sharia governance.
Experience with the regulation of tokenised assets and digital-asset custody.
Arabic language skills, both written and spoken.
Exposure to Omani law and experience working with Omani-admitted legal counsel.
Comfortable building legal frameworks and processes from the ground up, particularly where local precedent may not exist.
Commercially aware, with the ability to distinguish legal requirements from preferred approaches and explain the implications clearly.
A confident communicator who can advise and challenge senior stakeholders while building strong relationships across the business.
Willing to share knowledge and develop colleagues' understanding of the legal and regulatory environment.
Takes personal accountability for legal advice, drafting and decisions, including work prepared using approved technology and AI tools.
r: Establish the legal basis of the infrastructure: Ensure the enforceability of book-entry title, settlement finality and participant obligations under the law of the financial centre. Lead the preparation and maintenance of legal opinions relied upon by regulators and participants.

Lead regulatory engagement: Own the legal aspects of the company's authorisation and recognition processes, including regulatory applications, consultations on rules and regulations, and the ongoing supervisory relationship.

Develop the participant legal framework: Draft and maintain the rulebook, participation agreements and associated terms. Negotiate documentation with banks, custodians, participants and their legal advisers.

Manage commercial and outsourcing contracts: Take ownership of the company's legal contracts, particularly platform, technology and material outsourcing agreements, ensuring appropriate provisions covering service levels, liability, data protection and exit arrangements.
Support international recognition and access: Lead the legal work required for recognition by foreign authorities and facilitate cross-border participant access.
Advise on corporate governance and data matters: Provide legal advice on governance arrangements, delegated authority, internal policies, personal data protection and conflicts of interest.
Manage external legal advisers: Appoint and oversee external counsel, managing scope, budgets, quality and delivery.

Build the legal function: Establish the processes, records and controls needed to ensure that legal obligations, contracts and legal risks are properly documented and traceable within the company's operating model.
x: This is a rare opportunity to establish and lead the legal function of a new financial market infrastructure, shaping its regulatory and legal foundations from the outset and supporting its development into an operating institution.
